summary.text: 重 is used for “heavy” and “double; repeated.” Its origin remains disputed: a Han-dynasty dictionary analyzes 壬 as semantic and 東 as phonetic, while other proposals picture a person carrying a load or a sack above 土.

formation.text: The Han-dynasty dictionary records a phonosemantic analysis: 壬 contributes meaning and 東 supplies sound. Separate proposals interpret the graph as a person carrying a load or as a sack-like 東 above 土. The original construction is unresolved; the sack proposal does not establish that 土 was added later.

components.text: The Han-dynasty dictionary identifies 壬 as the semantic element in 重. This records that dictionary’s analysis, but does not establish the graph’s original referent.
The Han-dynasty dictionary assigns 東 a phonetic role. The supported reading pair below is modern; it does not independently prove that role or the ancient sound relationship.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin pair does not establish 東 as the phonetic element in this graph or prove an ancient sound relationship.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings differ; this pair does not demonstrate the historical analysis.

components.text: A competing account interprets 東 here as a sack, rather than as the dictionary’s sound element. That identification is not independently established.
In the sack account, 土 beneath 東 is interpreted as a weight. This proposed picture differs from the dictionary’s 壬-plus-東 analysis.

history.text: A bronze-script-style redraw shows a tall, bulbous form on the left and a branching form with several openings on the right. It is not tied to a dated inscription, so it does not establish an early form or a sequence of graphic changes.

The transmitted Han-dynasty dictionary analyzes 重 as 壬 semantic plus 東 phonetic. Other accounts picture a person carrying a load or a sack-like 東 above 土; neither the original referent nor a later addition of 土 is established.

An index lists Qin and Han materials, but no dated, contextual inscription was identified. The earliest secure graphic attestation remains unresolved. No object name or pronunciation is established for a proposed borrowing from a pictured load or sack.

uncertainties.text: The dictionary’s 壬-plus-東 analysis and the person-carrying-load and sack-and-weight proposals are distinct accounts; the evidence does not determine which explains the graph’s origin.
The original name or pronunciation of the proposed load or sack is not established, so borrowing the graph from such an object’s name is unsupported.
The timing and development of “thick/deep,” “heavy,” “weight,” “solemn/respectful,” and “repeat/overlap” are unresolved. The proposed relationship between 重 and 緟 is also unverified.

senses.period: Han-dynasty dictionary gloss; dating of word use unresolved
senses.text: The transmitted dictionary glosses 重 with 厚, “thick; deep.” This historical gloss is not an established earliest use or proof of the graph’s original meaning.
“Heavy” is a documented current meaning; its emergence relative to the dictionary gloss “thick; deep” is undated.
“Double” is a documented current meaning, and historical phonology data associate a reading with “repeat; double.” The evidence does not date this sense or show that it developed from “thick; deep.”
Historical phonology data record a noun meaning “weight”; its chronology relative to “heavy” is unresolved.
A historical commentary proposes this sense as an extension of “thick; deep,” but its timing is not established.

developments.text: A historical commentary links “solemn; respectful” to “thick; deep”; dated evidence for this development is unavailable.

limitations.text: The earliest dated use of the listed meanings is not identified. Dictionary glosses and reading metadata do not establish a chronology.
The proposal that 重 replaced 緟 for “overlap; repeat” is disputed and does not establish a semantic or graphic development.

overview.text: 重 means “heavy” or “double; repeated.” Its construction is disputed: an old dictionary analyzes 壬 as meaningful and 東 as a sound element; other proposals picture a person carrying a load or a sack above 土.

components.text: The dictionary assigns 壬 a semantic role in 重; “thick/deep” is the gloss for the whole character, but this does not settle what the original picture showed.
The dictionary treats 東 as a sound element; a separate proposal interprets it as part of a sack picture.
A separate, disputed account reads 東 as a sack.
In that disputed account, 土 below 東 is interpreted as a weight.

relationships.text: The Han-dynasty dictionary explicitly assigns 壬 a semantic role in 重; this records its analysis, not independent proof of the graph’s origin.
The Han-dynasty dictionary assigns 東 a phonetic role. Available current Mandarin readings differ and do not independently demonstrate the historical analysis.
A competing account interprets 東 as a sack in this graph, rather than as the dictionary’s phonetic element; that identification is not independently established.
